column1: # The documentation as wiki pages: the file in the repository, a tab, and the page it becomes.
# The page name is what a reader sees in the address bar and what a link between pages has to name, so
# this is the one place to look when a page is added, removed or renamed. A page name may not contain a
# space. Order here is the order the sidebar lists the pages in; the sidebar itself is wiki-sidebar.md,
# and both files have to agree, which the publishing script checks before it writes anything.
# The order is the reading order, not the order the pages were written in: what a menu and a window are,
# and which of the two modes a menu is built in, come before the syntax that writes them, so that the
# pages after them can be read without guessing at the model behind them.
# Both languages: a guide page is a pair, `<name>.zh-CN.md` and `<name>.md`, and each half carries the
# switch to the other on its first line. Chinese came first and keeps the plain page names; the English
# half takes the `-English` suffix, because the wiki is a single namespace.
# `docs/guide/…` is the syntax reference itself: the addon registers through Skript's addon API, which
# skUnity's automatic jar import cannot read (see CONTRIBUTION.md), so these pages are what a user reads
# instead. The README is the Home page and the entry point that points at them.
